verification_policy: These records are sourced from the structured research corpus and remain partially_verified until acquisition, mechanics, and CaC availability are independently reconciled against canonical in-game evidence.

records.name: Super God Fist
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 67 "Power of a Super Saiyan God"; the structured source reports a 27% Ultimate Finish reward slot. It is also listed in TP Medal Shop rotations for 30 TP Medals.
records.skill_description: A fast forward-charging Strike punch with grab properties that can connect through standing guard.
records.mechanics_notes: The research source describes a single-hit punch with long reach, fast startup, grab properties, and strong combo-linking utility. It can be used from basic strings and after teleport-style movement. The source reports community-measured damage of approximately 13–15%, which is retained as a measurement rather than an official damage value.
records.combo_notes: Useful as a combo ender or link after basic attacks and teleport movement; the grab property changes the usual guard interaction.
records.pve_notes: Provides a fast close-range finisher with reliable reach when an enemy is already positioned for a melee follow-up.
records.pvp_notes: The grab property means ordinary standing guard does not stop the hit, while the fast startup supports pressure and reaction-based confirms. Exact frame data is not established here.

records.name: Divine Retribution
records.unlock_method: TP Medal Shop limited-time rotation; the structured source lists a cost of 170 TP Medals while stocked.
records.skill_description: A branching Super that opens with a Ki Blast and can instead teleport above the target for a downward blade strike or spend additional Ki for a further attack.
records.mechanics_notes: The structured source documents three decision points: fire the initial blast, input before release to teleport above the opponent for a downward slice, and optionally spend more Ki after the blast for another attack. The research corpus describes the complete sequence as reaching roughly four hits at up to 200 Ki. Damage scaling is described as Strike despite the projectile opener.
records.combo_notes: The branching follow-ups give the move both a ranged opener and a teleporting close-range route; exact combo compatibility depends on target state and timing.
records.pve_notes: The multiple branches can adapt to enemy positioning, but the higher-Ki route should be treated as a resource-intensive option.
records.pvp_notes: The pre-release teleport branch changes the attack angle and can create a mix-up between the direct projectile and overhead-style approach. Exact frame data is not established here.

records.name: God of Destruction's Roar
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 105 "Champa's Hellish Holiday"; the structured source reports a 30% bonus-condition reward slot. It is also listed at 50 TP Medals in rotations.
records.skill_description: A sustained battle cry that forces the opponent to guard and warns that holding it too long leaves the user tired.
records.mechanics_notes: The source describes the move as dealing no direct health damage while forcing the target into guard stance. Community testing in the source reports rapid stamina drain during the forced guard. Holding the move extends the effect, but overextending triggers the user's tired state and a vulnerable recovery window.
records.combo_notes: This is primarily a setup and stamina-pressure tool rather than a conventional damage combo attack.
records.pve_notes: Can pressure AI-controlled enemies through forced guard and stamina depletion; the self-tired state makes prolonged use risky.
records.pvp_notes: Its forced-guard behavior creates stamina pressure, but the user must account for the punishable tired state if the roar is held too long.

records.name: Evil Eyes
records.unlock_method: Lord Slug Instructor Quest 1; the structured source describes it as a mentor-training reward and not a shop skill.
records.skill_description: A long-range eye attack that creates an explosion at the target's destination.
records.mechanics_notes: The research source describes a remote lock-on explosion positioned at the opponent's destination. It reports that the effect is not presented as a conventional projectile before detonation and that the resulting knockback moves the target toward the user. The source also reports stronger performance when used outside a combo or after knockback, but those damage measurements are community observations.
records.combo_notes: The reported toward-user knockback can convert a successful long-range hit into a close-range follow-up opportunity.
records.pve_notes: The destination-targeting behavior can catch moving AI opponents and create an approach opportunity after the hit.
records.pvp_notes: The delayed destination targeting can be useful against movement, while the lack of established frame data means exact punish and reaction windows remain unverified.

records.name: Savage Strike
records.unlock_method: TP Medal Shop limited-time rotation; the structured source lists 200 TP Medals while stocked.
records.skill_description: A long-distance lunging Strike punch with grab properties, plus an alternate teleport-above route when the additional input is made before startup.
records.mechanics_notes: The source documents a long forward lunge ending in a single grab-property punch and hard knockdown. An additional input before the move begins changes the route to a teleport above the opponent for an overhead strike. The source also reports that post-knockback use teleports to connect. Community-measured damage is approximately 15–20% and is not treated as an official value.
records.combo_notes: The direct version can chase knockbacks and end strings with a hard knockdown; the alternate route changes the attack angle before startup.
records.pve_notes: Long travel makes it useful for closing distance or following knockback states against enemies that remain within the move's targeting range.
records.pvp_notes: The grab property bypasses ordinary standing guard, while the alternate overhead route changes the opponent's defensive angle. The documented slower startup leaves an interruption risk that should not be overstated without frame data.
